title: Artificial Analysis 实测 GPT Image 2.6 图像生成与编辑表现
content:
Artificial Analysis 对 OpenAI 于 11 月 4 日发布的 GPT Image 2.6 进行了基准测试，两款模型在 AA-Image-T2I v2.1 和 AA-Image-Editing v2.1 上分列第一、二名。
独立实测给出两款模型的速度、质量与价格数据，读者可以据此在 Flare 和 Sunburst 之间做出选择。
OpenAI 的 GPT Image 2.6 在 AA-Image-T2I v2.1 和 AA-Image-Editing v2.1 两个榜单上均包揽第 1 和第 2 名。GPT Image 2.6 Flare 的速度几乎是 GPT Image 2.5 Flare 的两倍，质量还略有提升；而 GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst 则以更长的生成时间拿下榜首
OpenAI 于 11 月 4 日在 ChatGPT、Codex 和 API 中发布了 GPT Image 2.6。API 提供两个模型：GPT Image 2.6 Flare 和 GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst，分别接替 GPT Image 2.5 Flare 和 Sunburst。两者均支持文生图和图像编辑，并新增了动态 GIF 和 SVG 输出。OpenAI 在 API 中新增了复杂度设置，用于控制模型在渲染前进行多少规划。我们在最高质量下对两个模型进行了基准测试，复杂度采用 API 默认值 high。
在我们的测试中，GPT Image 2.6 Flare 的速度几乎是 GPT Image 2.5 Flare 的两倍，同时质量略有提升。其中位文生图生成时间从约 55 秒降至 30 秒，编辑时间从约 58 秒降至 32 秒。GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst 则相反：它比 GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst 更慢，每张图约需 2 分 15 秒，并拿下第 1 名。它在文生图方面提升最大的是推理、文字渲染、光照与材质，并且在 UIUX 设计方面表现最强。
两个模型的输出价格均为每 100 万图像输出 token 30 美元，与 GPT Image 2.5 相同。在最高质量下，这大约相当于每张 1024x1024 图像 0.21 美元（每 1000 张图像 211 美元）。
GPT Image 2.6 已在 ChatGPT 和 Codex 的所有层级以及 OpenAI API 中提供。
祝贺 @OpenAI 发布！

report.summary: Artificial Analysis benchmarked OpenAI's GPT Image 2.6 Flare and Sunburst, which swept first and second place on text-to-image and editing leaderboards, with Flare roughly twice as fast and Sunburst slower but highest quality.
report.background: OpenAI released GPT Image 2.6 on November 4 across ChatGPT, Codex and the API, shipping two variants — Flare for speed and Sunburst for maximum quality — that replace the 2.5 generation. The release lands in an increasingly crowded image-generation race, where Google's Gemini image models, Midjourney, Black Forest Labs and Chinese labs all compete on quality, latency and price. Independent leaderboards have become the de facto scoreboard for that competition: Artificial Analysis runs blind, standardized arenas (AA-Image-T2I and AA-Image-Editing, now at v2.1) that let buyers compare models on identical prompts rather than vendor demos. This update also adds structural features beyond raw pixels: animated GIF and SVG output, plus an API 'complexity' parameter that controls how much planning the model does before rendering — a lever that trades latency for fidelity and signals that inference-time reasoning is spreading from text models into image models.
key_points: GPT Image 2.6 took both first and second place on Artificial Analysis' text-to-image (AA-Image-T2I v2.1) and image-editing (AA-Image-Editing v2.1) leaderboards, with the slower Sunburst variant at number one overall.

Flare is the speed play: median text-to-image time fell from about 55 to 30 seconds and editing from about 58 to 32 seconds versus GPT Image 2.5 Flare — nearly two times faster — while quality edged slightly upward.

Sunburst is the quality play: it is slower than its predecessor at roughly 2 minutes 15 seconds per image, but shows the biggest gains in reasoning, text rendering, lighting and materials, and is strongest at UI/UX design tasks.
Pricing is unchanged from GPT Image 2.5 at $30 per million image output tokens, roughly $0.21 per 1024x1024 image ($211 per 1,000 images) at the highest quality setting used in testing.

The API adds GIF animation and SVG output plus a 'complexity' setting controlling pre-render planning; benchmarks used the default 'high' at maximum quality, meaning real-world latency and cost can be tuned down.
report.impact: The results confirm a maturing market split into tiers rather than a single best model: buyers can now pick a fast tier for high-volume iteration and a slow tier for final assets, with identical pricing across both. That is good news for product teams building design tools, ad pipelines and UI mockup generators, where a 30-second turnaround changes whether generation feels interactive. For developers, the new complexity knob and SVG/GIF outputs mean image models are becoming programmable pipelines rather than one-shot endpoints, but the unchanged per-token price keeps cost pressure on. For regular users, gains show up as better in-image text and UI renders inside ChatGPT — practical for slides and mockups — while the real competitive question shifts to whether Google and open-weight rivals respond on price.
report.tools: Track Artificial Analysis' Image Arena leaderboards for apples-to-apples comparisons of quality, latency and price. Try the two variants directly via the OpenAI API playground or in ChatGPT and Codex; read the API docs for the new complexity setting, GIF and SVG outputs. For open-weight alternatives and local experimentation, watch ComfyUI and Hugging Face Diffusers, which usually add new model support quickly, and compare hosted pricing on fal.ai or Replicate before committing to a pipeline.
